name: What is the difference between direct fixture replacement and relocating fixtures?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between direct fixture replacement and relocating fixtures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a fixture in the exact same footprint only involves disconnecting old lines and connecting the new unit to existing rough plumbing. Moving a fixture requires opening walls or subfloors to extend supply lines, re-sloping waste drain lines for proper gravity flow, and adjusting atmospheric vent stacks. For toilets, moving location requires maintaining a precise downward slope toward the main soil stack, which can be limited by floor joist direction. A direct replacement minimizes drywall repairs and keeps labor timelines short.
acceptedAnswer.description: Direct replacement connects to existing plumbing in place. Relocating requires opening floors or walls to reroute supply, drain, and vent piping.
